title: Read wants and their decision associations
summary: Read active or archived wants, accepted decisions, Annals evidence and graph history, and intake handoff progress.
use_when: Captured wants, their associated decisions, source evidence, history, or outstanding processing should be inspected.
do_not_use_when: New model work, source capture, graph changes, deployment, or scheduling is requested.
outcome: A read of selected local intake and available Annals library records, with their different freshness boundaries visible.
effects: Reads local intake and supported Annals views.
Starts no model and changes no domain records.
authority: Conatus owns intake and handoff facts. Annals owns work, evidence, concept and revision facts.
success: The response identifies the selected input or requested collection and separates missing Annals state from local capture.
failure_and_recovery: A failed Annals read does not erase captured input or prove failed interpretation. Inspect library and inbox state when the dependency is available.
privacy: Responses may include complete want wording, decision fields, source references, and exact evidence. Do not publish them implicitly.
does_not_authorize: Publishing private content, directly editing Annals state, or changing unrelated product state.

access.statement: The current local user invokes the Conatus CLI. --state-dir selects private Conatus state. No remote API or multi-user authorization surface is provided.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Contract 2 makes want lists active-only by default, adds --archived and --all, adds want record.state and status local.wants counts. The database remains schema 1; existing wants default to active.
No general cross-release compatibility or deprecation window is promised.

Contract 3 requires --json for the ordinary CLI machine response. The prior JSON success and error shapes and their streams are preserved with that flag. Default readable text does not change persistent state formats or the separate installation and status-snapshot protocols.

operational_limits.statement: Intake lists default to 20 and accept 1 through 100. Graph and association previews return at most 200 concepts and at most 20 parents, children and evidence entries per concept; completeness flags identify bounded coverage.
Storage capacity and wall-clock completion bounds are not specified.

consumers.statement: A local user or agent reads captured wants, accepted decision documents, their Annals organization, or processing state.

preconditions.statement: Conatus state is initialized. Annals-backed reads also require the configured Annals executable and pinned named library to be readable.

inputs.statement: want or decision list selects a source kind with --limit; show selects one intake ID. graph selects the current Annals graph. history selects a bounded Annals revision history. status selects current local intake and available inbox state. Want lists default to active; mutually exclusive --archived and --all select archived or both states.

outputs.statement: Commands print readable text by default. --json selects the existing {ok:true,data:...} machine response. Human and JSON errors go to stderr with a nonzero exit; JSON errors retain {ok:false,error:string}. Lists default to 20 records and allow 1 through 100. A selected intake show separates record, retention, interpretation, and associations; each remote read has available data or its own error. Annals unavailability is reported separately from locally retained input. Want records include state: active or archived. Status local.wants contains active and archived counts, including zero. Record fields preserve exact wording/document and source_data. related_records projects only intake grounded in the returned association graph and shares its completeness flags. Human intake lists use summary rows and identify more results; show reads preserve full wording, observations, evidence and completeness fields.

data_semantics.statement: Captured wants are source assertions. New decision intake preserves unchanged Annals document text and original transport event; earlier structured projections remain historical sources with only their available context. Graph edges express source-grounded interpretation under selected instructions, not progress or current force.
Lifecycle state belongs only to the Conatus want. Archived means inactive, not completed. Its captured content stays immutable; Annals processing and associations remain independent and can evolve.

identity_and_units.statement: Local IDs distinguish want and decision inputs; decision IDs are decision- followed by SHA-256 of source library ID, colon, and event ID. Annals concept IDs, work names, revisions, and feed event/account IDs retain their separate namespaces. Intake timestamps are UTC Unix seconds; source occurrence precision is preserved. Feed accepted_at describes Annals acceptance rather than decision occurrence.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Lists select retained Conatus intake by source kind. Status counts name the intake kind and queued or pending handoff selection. The stored cursor marks consumed decision-feed coverage, not interpreted coverage. Graph bounds and Annals current reads retain Annals semantics; a recent graph revision does not prove all captured inputs were interpreted. Want state selection precedes limits and has_more. Existing intake and handoff counts include both states. Show can select either state.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Reads start no model and do not change intake, library instructions, source retention, or the corpus. Local and Annals reads are not one cross-system snapshot.

reliances.statement: Graph, history, work and association reads use the selected Annals corpus interfaces.
